name: 20 Microns Ltd
tagline: India's largest micronized-minerals maker, dirt-cheap at ~12x P/E, slowly shifting mix from commodity (paints-linked) toward value-added specialty minerals and functional additives -- EBITDA margin is inflecting up (Q1 FY27 op margin 13.2% vs 12.2% QoQ) even through a weak paints cycle, but revenue has now stalled (Q1 FY27 flat YoY, not just paints), FY25 FCF was negative, and related-party / remuneration governance niggles recur
business_overview: 20 Microns (20ML) mines and micronizes industrial minerals -- calcium carbonate, kaolin, talc, etc. -- from mine to sub-micron/nano sizing, India's largest producer of micronized industrial minerals. End-markets: paints (~46-48% of sales), polymers/plastics (~25%), rubber (~9%), plus ceramics/construction. Strategy is a multi-year 'evolution' toward Performance Minerals, specialty chemicals and functional additives (higher margin, longer approval cycles, stickier). Backward integration via ~11.3 MT captive mine reserves and a new Malaysian mine; nano subsidiary (20MNML) now ~100% owned.
fundamentals_table: Revenue ~Rs 954 Cr (+~18% reported, flattered by consolidation); PAT Rs 66.7 Cr (+6.7% YoY); EBITDA margin ~12.9%
Net sales Rs 244.7 Cr (-1% YoY, -6% QoQ); PAT Rs 17.8 Cr (+5.5% YoY); op margin 13.24% vs 12.17% QoQ
EBITDA/op margin inflecting up (~12.2->13.2% recent quarters) despite paints price war
FY25 FCF ~ -Rs 45 Cr; CFO fell ~49% FY23->FY25 (Rs 63->Rs 32 Cr); inventory days ~88
Net debt ~Rs 65 Cr; Debt/EBITDA ~1.3x; Rs 100 Cr capex / 24 months (40% Malaysia @70:30 equity:debt, rest accruals)
18-22% revenue CAGR over 3-5 yrs (aspirational); +200-250 bps margin; ROCE 18-20%; 20%+ high-value-product share by FY30; no explicit FY27 number
fundamentals_narrative: The margin/mix inflection is real and continuing -- FY26 EBITDA margin held ~12.9-13.6% through the Birla-Opus paints price war, and Q1 FY27 operating margin stepped up to 13.24% from 12.17% QoQ, with finance costs falling. But the growth side has weakened: FY26 reported revenue +~18% was flattered by consolidation/acquisitions, and Q1 FY27 net sales were -1% YoY and -6% QoQ -- i.e. flat now applies to the whole book, not just paints. Cash conversion is poor: FY25 free cash flow was about -Rs 45 Cr on Rs 62 Cr PAT, operating cash flow fell ~49% FY23->FY25, inventory days rose to ~88. Malaysian limestone mine (11 MT reserves, ~Rs 27 Cr) is in mining-prep, operational early FY27; Sievert construction-chemicals JV plant inaugurated; Rs 100 Cr / 24-month capex underway (40% Malaysia, 70:30 equity:debt; domestic via accruals). A Rs 1.25 FY26 dividend re-initiates payouts after several dry years. Governance niggles persist: Rs 50 Cr enabling approval for a loan to a promoter-interested entity (loan agreement executed Mar-2026 with a subsidiary), director/family remuneration ~12% of PAT rising ~25% YoY, deposits from promoter relatives, two independent directors retired leaving only two.
technical_read: Not pulled. 52-week range ~Rs 130-284; was put under ASM/T2T in late 2024 after a >150% run (no fundamental trigger).
sentiment_summary: Active thread; anchor bull is pranavpallod12 (trusted, elevated) for whom 20ML is the single biggest portfolio position by cost. His thesis, repeated with quarterly updates: cheap valuation caps downside, margins inflecting, mix shifting to value-added, Malaysian mines for cost-side moat in the commodity book, backward integration reduces freight/RM volatility. A Financial Express 'hidden gems' piece (Dec-2025) framed the same 'boring mineral company quietly becoming a specialty play' narrative. Pushback: Malolan_R notes calcium carbonate is abundant / low value-add and China is a big player; Aman_Jain3, Jagdish85, Investsafe and akshay_awasthi press hard on the Rs 50 Cr related-party loan and on family remuneration (~Rs 7.5 Cr / 12% of PAT), several e-mailing IR and getting only standard responses. Management gave no FY27 guidance ('uncertainty'), near term called 'hazy'.
community_signal: One trusted (elevated) user holds a large, openly-disclosed conviction position and updates the thread every quarter with a constructive thesis; no trusted user is bearish. Governance concerns are raised by non-trusted posters. Net: positive trusted signal at elevated tier (not core, no floor).

trusted_signals.note: Biggest position by cost; thesis 'completely intact, in fact improving' -- margin expansion through weak paints cycle, mix shift to value-added, Malaysian mines for backward integration
Post-FY26: 'valuations remain dirt-cheap, capping downside'; re-rating only when 15-20% steady growth + margin improvement shows over multiple quarters

bse_notes: No corporate-action red flags. Governance watch-items: Rs 50 Cr enabling approval for loan to promoter-interested entity (stated to be routed only to subsidiaries; loan agreement executed Mar-2026 with a subsidiary); director+family remuneration ~12% of PAT, up ~25% YoY; fixed deposits taken from promoter relatives; sparse concalls in some quarters.

value_chain.theme: China-beating specialty minerals / functional additives (import-substitution + export)
value_chain.position: Largest Indian micronized-minerals producer, mine-to-nano; supplier into paints, polymers, rubber, ceramics -- moving up into performance minerals and functional additives
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Captive mineral reserves + micronization/surface-treatment know-how and multi-year customer approvals for specialty grades
value_chain.note: Commodity ~80% of the book (cost-driven, China-exposed); thesis rides on the ~20% value-added slice compounding faster and lifting blended margin. Malaysian mine + captive reserves are the cost-side lever in the commodity book.

bull_case: Cheap: ~12x P/E, ~1.7x P/B, ~5x EV/EBITDA for a market-leading, asset-backed minerals franchise
Margin inflection continuing: Q1 FY27 operating margin 13.24% vs 12.17% QoQ, through a brutal paints price war
Value-added segments (polymers, rubber, exports, specialty) structurally outgrowing the commodity paints book
Backward integration (captive reserves ~11 MT + Malaysian limestone mine, operational early FY27) is a real cost-side lever
FY26 dividend re-initiated (Rs 1.25) after several dry years; trusted (elevated) user holds it as top position and updates constructively
bear_case: Growth has stalled: Q1 FY27 revenue -1% YoY / -6% QoQ -- flat now applies to the whole book, not just paints
FY25 free cash flow ~ -Rs 45 Cr; operating cash flow down ~49% FY23->FY25; working-capital / inventory bloat
~80% of the book is commodity minerals with limited value-add and Chinese competition
Recurring governance drags: Rs 50 Cr related-party loan (executed Mar-2026), family remuneration ~12% of PAT +25%/yr, FDs from promoter relatives, two IDs retired
No explicit FY27 guidance; re-rating needs 15-20% sustained growth that has moved further away, not closer
verdict_headline: A cheap, market-leading minerals franchise where the margin/mix inflection is real but revenue has now stalled -- kept at 10x-in-2-3-years on valuation + moat, cut to Low-Medium conviction, 'unconfirmed' until growth resumes past ~15%
verdict_reasoning: Per the open-screen rule against letting a flat trailing average hide an inflection: EBITDA/operating margin is demonstrably turning up through a weak cycle (Q1 FY27 13.24% vs 12.17% QoQ), and there are dated catalysts (Malaysian mine early FY27, Rs 100 Cr capex, Sievert construction-chemicals JV). Cheap valuation (four_box valuation=yes) plus a genuine cost/know-how moat (four_box moat=yes) keep four_box at 3.0 and the 10x-in-2-3-years label permitted.

But conviction moves Medium -> Low-Medium: the deep read confirms revenue has decelerated to roughly flat YoY (Q1 FY27 -1%), FY25 free cash flow was negative (~ -Rs 45 Cr) on working-capital bloat, and the governance drags are unchanged. The re-rating trigger -- sustained 15-20% growth -- is further away than a year ago.

Red-flag check: none. The Rs 50 Cr related-party loan (executed Mar-2026 with a subsidiary) and elevated family remuneration are real governance drags that cap conviction, but do not meet AVOID / HIGH CAUTION / EXCLUDE definitions.

Re-check on FY27 prints for (a) blended EBITDA margin holding past ~14%, (b) revenue growth actually resuming, (c) Malaysian mine commissioning and its cost impact, (d) any escalation of the related-party loan or remuneration.
disclaimer: This is independent research for informational purposes only, not investment advice.

four_box.note: ~80% of book remains commodity minerals (China-exposed) and Q1 FY27 revenue was flat YoY, so tailwind/tam marked weak despite the value-added mix-shift; captive reserves + micronization know-how + multi-year customer approvals are a real moat; ~12x P/E / ~1.7x P/B / ~5x EV-EBITDA is explicitly cheap -- valuation yes. Score 3.0 keeps 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction held at Low-Medium 'unconfirmed' because growth has stalled and FCF is negative.
